title: [翻译] 长生草属【不能说包罗万象的】总介绍

segments.t: 原创翻译，禁止无授权转载。 （有些对中国环境下帮助不大的我会略去不翻） 说好的翻译在这里~这是我的第一次 长生草是一种起源于欧洲大陆的植物。被发现于高海拔地区（即高山地带）。他们生长在严酷而崎岖的地形环境中。 长生草在美国正变得越来越受欢迎，多肉爱好者们纷纷爱上了这种神奇的小植物的花纹和颜色。 在网上，多肉爱好者们正渐渐引进长生草属。他们被广泛用于各色园艺——美化墙壁，居家绿植，建造庞大的多肉花环以及被放在新颖的容器中试栽培。（你应去）了解关于这些萌物的相关资料，并且学着如何照顾她们。这将帮助确保你能让她们好好在你家成长。 （略） 把握到了种植要领后，长生草可以在相当广泛的美国地区茁壮生长。 （略） 在他们的原产地，许多地方的土壤肥力相当小，这使得它们适合制作和拼盘（Wassily1890的话：因为生存力强 ）。 他们需要在能快速排水的土壤以及拥有充足的阳光的环境下生长。 夏季，在炎热地区的极端酷暑/干燥的对流风条件下适当遮阴最好。 这些令人惊奇的植物的叶子都拥有广泛的颜色：绿、金、赤、橙、紫、巧克力色和棕褐色。每种颜色深浅各不相同，它们以各种形式被显现在长生草属的叶片上。叶子的颜色会随着季节的推移而渐渐改变。叶的纹理或光滑或丝绒感强。植株大小也各不相等，小至1/8''，大至10''以上。 在他们的栖息地，长生草属收到在夏季能获得的水分很少，而在漫长的冬天，他们常常会被白雪所覆盖（Wassily1890的话：所以耐寒力很强 ）。浇水时，注意不要浇透。You want the water to drain fairly quickly and the soil to be somewhat dry by the next day. （Wassily1890的话：这句话好奇怪 ）。如果你家属于又热又湿的环境，而当树叶开始出现脱水的迹象时，最好是少浇水。你应该在凉爽的黄昏浇水。太多的水也是一个问题。 （略） Sempervivums, Jovibarba hirta, and Jovibarba globifera reproduce by offsets attached to a stolon. The stolons of these Jovibarba are fragile and break easily, allowing the tiny offsets to roll away from the parent rosette before forming roots. This is how they earned their common name of ‘Rollers.’ Each rosette will live for several years before flowering. By then, you will have many new plants. Jovibarba heuffelii do not reproduce by offsets. Instead, they produce new rosettes within the mother plant's crown and thick root system.  These must be divided with a knife by cutting through the crown and root. Each new plant must contain a piece of healthy root and crown in order to survive on its own.（Wassily1890的话：这两大段好艰难 ） 最后是长生草属植株的细分介绍：

这是一篇相当不成熟的文章，仓促之下翻译的，不要打我！！ 能看懂是第一目的。 原文：Sempervivums are plants that originate on the European continent. Found at high altitudes known as alpine zones, they thrive in this harsh and rugged terrain. Sempervivums are becoming increasingly popular in the United States as gardeners fall in love with the textures and colors of these amazing little plants. All over the Internet, gardeners are being introduced to Sempervivums. Their uses include topiaries, living walls, living wreaths, and a vast array of  creative container gardening ideas. Learning about these small beauties and how to care for them will help ensure your success in incorporating them into your gardens. Sempervivums are known by the common names of "Hens and Chicks" and "Houseleeks," as well as other lesser known names. Jovibarba are a close relative of Sempervivum and may also be known as "Rollers" or "Beard of Jupiter."  With the proper care, these plants can be grown in a wide range of US zones: from zone 3 up to zone 9. In their native habitat, many grow on rocks with minimal soil available, which makes them ideal for crafting and container gardening. They do require fast-draining soil and lots of sun.  In areas with extreme summer heat and/or drying wind conditions, afternoon shade or filtered light would be best. These amazing plants come in a wide range of leaf colors: green, gold, red, orange, purple, chocolate, and tan, in many different shades of each color and combinations of various colors.  Many change color from one season to another. Leaf textures range from smooth to webby or fuzzy.  Size varies from 1/8" or less across a rosette, to 10" or more. In their native habitat, Sempervivums receive little moisture in the summer and are covered in snow for the long winter months. When watering, don’t saturate the soil. You want the water to drain fairly quickly and the soil to be somewhat dry by the next day. You’ll know to irrigate if the leaves start to show signs of dehydration. It is best to water them sparingly if you have a combination of hot and humid conditions.  In hot and dry conditions, you should water in the cool of the evening. Too much water is also a problem. A top dressing of grit/pea gravel keeps the leaves from rotting during the periods of heavy rainfall I have in winter and spring in the Pacific Northwest. Sempervivums, Jovibarba hirta, and Jovibarba globifera reproduce by offsets attached to a stolon. The stolons of these Jovibarba are fragile and break easily, allowing the tiny offsets to roll away from the parent rosette before forming roots. This is how they earned their common name of ‘Rollers.’ Each rosette will live for several years before flowering. By then, you will have many new plants. Jovibarba heuffelii do not reproduce by offsets. Instead, they produce new rosettes within the mother plant's crown and thick root system.  These must be divided with a knife by cutting through the crown and root. Each new plant must contain a piece of healthy root and crown in order to survive on its own.(by valleylynn)
